items.claim: checkJustTokenProvider counts any non-empty auth parameter, so Gitea/Sourcehut pass validation with only the API URL set, while collectProviderBackupResults requires the token (pre-existing, carried into the new helper).
items.consequence: GIT_BACKUP_DIR and GITEA_APIURL set, GITEA_TOKEN unset: checkProvidersDefined gets count=1 and passes, no provider runs, the log says 'all backups failed', a 'failed' notification is sent, and the one-shot process exits 0 because failed == 0.

items.claim: checkProvidersDefined intercepts both BitBucket providers before checkProvider, so partial BitBucket credentials are never reported and the BitBucket entries in userAndPasswordProviders are dead (pre-existing, kept by the refactor).
items.consequence: GITHUB_TOKEN plus BITBUCKET_USER and BITBUCKET_KEY set, BITBUCKET_SECRET missing: validation passes with no 'parameter is not defined' error (Azure DevOps would get one), and BitBucket is silently never backed up.

items.claim: displayBitBucketStartupConfig gates only on BITBUCKET_EMAIL instead of the new bitbucketAPITokenDefined() || bitbucketOAuthDefined() predicate, so the startup log disagrees with what actually runs.
items.consequence: OAuth2 users (BITBUCKET_USER/KEY/SECRET, no email) get no BitBucket backups-to-keep, compare-method or LFS lines although BitBucket is backed up; a user with only BITBUCKET_EMAIL sees 'BitBucket compare method: clone' although BitBucket is skipped.

items.claim: validateStartupConfig reads GIT_BACKUP_DIR with os.LookupEnv and returns a newline-trimmed path used only by createWorkingDir; displayStartupConfig and runProviderBackups re-read it via GetEnvOrFile (pre-existing, now fixed in place by the extracted signature).
items.consequence: With only GIT_BACKUP_DIR_FILE set, startup logs 'root backup directory: /backups' and then Run fails with 'environment variable GIT_BACKUP_DIR must be set'. With GIT_BACKUP_DIR='/backups\n', validation and the working dir use '/backups' but the backup run targets '/backups\n'.

items.claim: scheduleBackups creates a gocron scheduler before deciding whether one is needed; the one-shot default branch never uses or shuts it down.
items.consequence: With no interval or cron set, every Run() allocates a scheduler and its goroutines that are never released (accumulating across repeated Run() calls in tests), and a NewScheduler error would abort a one-shot backup that needs no scheduler. Moving NewScheduler into runScheduledJob removes this.

items.claim: Bitbucket() still carries its own copy of the API-token/OAuth2 completeness check instead of calling the new bitbucketAPITokenDefined()/bitbucketOAuthDefined() helpers.
items.consequence: The predicate now lives in two places (helpers in backup.go, inline in bitbucket.go:15-26). A change to one, such as trimming whitespace or adding a credential, makes collectProviderBackupResults invoke Bitbucket() which then returns 'authentication not properly configured', or the reverse.

items.claim: The new tokenProviders table is another hand-maintained provider registry alongside enabledProviderAuth, justTokenProviders/userAndPasswordProviders and the five display*StartupConfig functions.
items.consequence: The lists already disagree: Sourcehut is backed up but has no startup-config display, and validation and execution use different 'configured' rules. Adding a provider means editing four places. A single provider descriptor (name, gating env vars, run func, display options) would let validation, display and execution share one definition.

items.claim: The logger uses log.Lshortfile, so moving the startup log calls into shared helpers changes the file:line prefix; the PR's 'log output unchanged' claim is not strictly true.
items.consequence: 'GitHub/Gitea/GitLab/BitBucket/Azure DevOps compare method' lines, and likewise the orgs, backups-to-keep and LFS lines, now all report the same helper line number instead of a per-provider one. Anything matching on the prefix, or a person using it to locate the provider block, is affected.

items.claim: The simplified TestGiteaOrgsRepositoryBackup still calls resetBackups() inside each switch case and again immediately after the switch.
items.consequence: Backups are reset twice per iteration, plus the deferred reset. Dropping the per-case calls gives the same behaviour with less code, which was the point of this refactor.

items.claim: The rewritten RUN keeps `rm -f "/var/cache/apk/*"`, whose quoted glob never expands and which is redundant with `apk add --no-cache` (as is `--update`).
items.consequence: The command tries to delete a file literally named '*' and removes nothing. It is dead weight in an instruction the PR edited specifically to satisfy Dockerfile lint rules; drop it or unquote the glob.
